register.name: Revised Flash Appeal for Lebanon, March to August 2026
register.detail: United Nations and humanitarian partners · Launched 13 March 2026 at $308.3 million for three months · Revised to cover June to August 2026
register.text: The UN-coordinated humanitarian appeal for Lebanon, launched on 13 March 2026 for one million people over three months and revised to cover March to August 2026. It sought $639.9 million for multi-sector assistance to 1.4 million vulnerable people, the emergency layer beneath the seven standards.

register.name: UNICEF Humanitarian Action for Children, Lebanon 2026
register.text: UNICEF’s humanitarian appeal for Lebanon in 2026, revised in April 2026. It seeks $388.5 million to reach 2 million people, including 700,000 children.

register.name: Lebanon Digital Acceleration Project
register.detail: World Bank · P506791 · Approved 26 January 2026 · Signed 10 August 2026 at the Ministry of Finance · To go to Parliament for final approval
register.note: Part of the $350 million approved in January 2026; the signing is reported by The National and L’Orient-Le Jour
register.text: World Bank financing for the digital transformation of the public sector: secure hosting of government data, cybersecurity and the digitisation of select public services. Better public services and data make every one of the seven standards easier to deliver and to measure.

register.name: Social Safety Net Enhancement and System Building Project
register.note: Part of the $350 million approved in January 2026
register.text: World Bank financing that continues cash transfers to poor and vulnerable Lebanese households and strengthens the social protection delivery system, including the DAEM platform as a social registry. Cash transfers carry the poorest households toward the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP)
register.detail: World Bank · P509428 · Approved 24 June 2025 · Initial financing of a US$1 billion scalable framework · $750 million still to be mobilised from partners
register.note: Damage estimated at US$7.2 billion and recovery needs at US$11 billion (World Bank)
register.text: The first financing for the repair and reconstruction of damaged critical public infrastructure and lifeline services in conflict-affected areas, including rubble management with reuse and recycling. It restores water, energy, mobility, health and education services, four of which are among the seven standards.

register.name: Second Greater Beirut Water Supply Project
register.detail: IBRD loan 97690 · P504170 · Approved 14 January 2025 · Effective 27 February 2026 · Closing 31 December 2032
register.note: 0.25% disbursed by April 2026 (World Bank status report)
register.text: World Bank financing to complete critical water infrastructure, improve water quality and reduce reliance on costly private water sources for 1.8 million people in Greater Beirut and Mount Lebanon. Only 47.7% of Lebanese use safely managed drinking water: this project carries the water standard.

register.name: Renewable Energy and System Reinforcement Project
register.detail: IBRD loan 9731 · Approved 1 October 2024 · Signed 16 April 2025 · Closing 31 December 2030 · About 150 MW of utility-scale solar
register.note: Effectiveness not confirmed in the documents opened
register.text: An IBRD loan to enable cleaner, more reliable and efficient grid electricity in Lebanon, with about 150 MW of utility-scale solar power and grid reinforcement for Électricité du Liban. The grid supplies about one third of national demand: this project carries the energy standard.

register.name: Fiscal Management Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 14 February 2024 · $28.5 million IBRD loan and $5.5 million Lebanon Financing Facility grant, a $34 million project
register.note: Ministry of Finance, Court of Accounts and Central Inspection
register.text: A World Bank project to restore core public financial management: revenue and customs administration, budget preparation, fiscal reporting and timely public payments. A working treasury is the base on which the state finances the seven standards.

register.name: EU support for Lebanon, 2026 and 2027
register.detail: European Commission · Announced 24 September 2026, New York · Second part of a €1 billion package for 2024 to 2027 · First €500 million adopted in August 2024
register.note: Basic services, recovery and reforms, civil society and culture
register.text: The second part of the European Union’s €1 billion package for Lebanon, for 2026 and 2027. It maintains access to education, health, social protection and water, with cash assistance for vulnerable households and primary healthcare, and supports reforms, security and recovery in conflict-affected areas.

register.name: Six EU grant agreements on security, recovery and reforms
register.detail: European Union · Signed 14 January 2026 · €30 million Internal Security Forces · €25 million border management · €25 million local recovery · €13.5 million anti-corruption · €9 million public services · €8 million energy for security institutions
register.text: Six EU grants signed with Lebanon for security, recovery and reforms. €25 million promotes local recovery and resilience in conflict-affected areas and €9 million helps ministries deliver more modern public services; most of the rest strengthens security institutions.

register.name: Spinneys Lebanon, food retail and energy efficiency
register.detail: EBRD · 20 May 2026 · $20.5 million senior loan and $1.5 million co-investment grant · EU first-loss guarantee under EFSD+
register.note: Borrower Spinneys Levant Limited, through Gray Mackenzie Retail Lebanon SAL
register.text: EBRD financing for the Spinneys food retail chain to expand its stores and production, including a fresh snack production line, and to fund energy-efficiency measures across its outlets. It supports the supply of food and is expected to save 150,844.66 GJ of energy a year.

register.name: BCI Holding, loan for manufacturing expansion
register.detail: IFC · 20 November 2025 · Loan of up to $40 million · Includes an R&D and Innovation Center
register.text: An IFC loan to BCI Holding S.A. to support its expansion in Lebanon and the Middle East. IFC expects it to drive job creation and the development of small and medium enterprises, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Matelec, investment for infrastructure projects
register.detail: IFC · 20 November 2025 · Investment of up to $30 million · Instrument not stated
register.text: An IFC investment in Matelec to support the company’s upcoming infrastructure projects in Lebanon and the wider Middle East and North Africa. IFC links it to industrial development and job creation, the livelihood standard.

register.name: Lebanon MF Support Facility: Al Majmoua and Vitas
register.detail: IFC · Approved 31 July 2025 · Invested 6 November 2025 · Two senior loans totalling $10 million · First-loss guarantee of up to $5 million through the PROSPECTS facility
register.text: Two IFC senior loans to the microfinance lenders Al Majmoua and Vitas, for micro, small and medium enterprises and women entrepreneurs, with a focus on forcibly displaced people and host communities. Small loans preserve and create jobs, the livelihood standard.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2023
items.text: Lebanese abroad send back a third of the economy: the nation’s deepest capital.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Byblos, Baalbek, the mountains and the coast: visitors earn more than a quarter of exports.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: The Bekaa valley’s vineyards, orchards and grain.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: The cedar forests: a symbol, a watershed and a living asset.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 25.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Souk el Tayeb
items.text: A farmers’ market founded in 2004 by Kamal Mouzawak that has grown into restaurants, community kitchens and guest houses, with 65 to 70 vendors at its Saturday market in Mar Mikhael, Beirut.

items.name: YY ReGen
items.text: A Beirut start-up that rents its ReGen-R8 on-demand solar energy systems to farmers and rural businesses as a service, so they avoid the upfront cost of solar; all ten of its units were rented out in October 2024.

items.name: Lebanese Alternative Learning
items.text: An ed-tech social enterprise whose Tabshoura platform puts Lebanon’s primary curriculum online, free, in three languages, and has reached more than 65,000 underserved children, with a financial sustainability arm, ConsultEd Solutions.

items.name: arcenciel
items.text: A Lebanese non-profit whose healthcare waste unit treats around 13 tonnes of healthcare waste a day by shredding and steam sterilisation at three centres, in partnership with over 90% of the nation’s hospitals, laboratories and care centres.

items.name: Al Majmoua
items.text: The Lebanese Association for Development, a non-profit lender to micro, small and medium enterprises and women entrepreneurs, which received IFC senior loans in November 2025 to lend to displaced people and host communities.

items.name: Nadeera
items.text: A social enterprise that tackles waste in Lebanon through its Yalla Return service, whose franchise model lets local entrepreneurs set up buy-back centres, and that designs waste systems for municipalities.
